sections.overview: This lizard-cuckoo is endemic to Puerto Rico and closely related to Cuba’s C. merlini.
sections.identification: Its long tail has white-tipped outer feathers, and the bill is dark above with a yellow lower edge.
sections.habitat: It uses forests, dense suburban vegetation, shade-coffee plantations and even dry woodland.
sections.diet: Lizards are its main prey, supplemented by large spiders, insects and small frogs.
sections.behavior: It forages slowly and quietly through the understory and canopy, using stealth to approach prey.
sections.reproduction: Breeding occurs year-round, with most activity from March to June; the nest is a loose structure of leaves and sticks.
sections.ecology: It shares the Caribbean lizard-cuckoo group with C. merlini, but the two are island endemics on different islands.
sections.conservation: The Puerto Rico atlas reports Least Concern globally and no local threatened-category listing in its cited assessment.
